---
title: Offline Sync
description: What a device does without a connection, and how it catches up.
---

Fieldkit is built for places without signal. A device answers surveys, stores submissions and queues uploads locally, and syncs whenever a connection appears.

## How Sync Works

Each sync does three things in order:

1. **Upload** pending submissions, oldest first, with their attachments
2. **Download** survey versions and settings changed since the last sync
3. **Report** health signals (battery, storage, clock skew)

A sync that is interrupted resumes from the last submission that was acknowledged. Nothing is uploaded twice.

:::note
Attachments are uploaded after the submission that references them. A submission can therefore appear in the dashboard a few seconds before its photos do.
:::

### Before a trip without signal

- [x] Publish the survey version the team will answer
- [ ] Sync every device while it still has a connection
- [ ] Check each device's free storage against the photos you expect
- [ ] Raise `sync_interval` if the trip is longer than the auto-sleep interval

## Sync Interval

Devices try to sync every `sync_interval` minutes while connected, and immediately when a connection returns after an outage. See [Device Management](/docs/device-management#device-settings) for how to change it.

## Storage on the Device

Pending submissions are kept until they are acknowledged. Synced submissions are kept for `retention_days` so the team can review them in the field.

When the device's `storage_quota` is full, the app refuses new submissions with a warning rather than discarding old ones.

## Conflicts

Two devices can edit the same record — for example, a site visited twice in one day. Fieldkit keeps both submissions and marks the later one as a revision of the earlier, by `device_time`.

:::caution
Revision order uses the **device** clock. A device with large clock skew can make an old visit look like the latest one. Check `clock_skew` in [health signals](/docs/device-management#health-signals).
:::

## Forcing a Sync

```bash
fieldkit devices sync tablet-07
```

The request is delivered as a push notification; a device without a connection picks it up when it next has one.
